append.text: **Ps 5:2, its first place:** *Dai ouvidos, Senhor, às minhas palavras* — holds; natural order (MS1932 has the same words); Latinist clean, stylist and blind reader silent. It stands there beside *intéllege* → *entendei* and *inténde* → *atendei*, three verbs kept three.
Ps 5:3 *Atendei à voz da minha oração* — the stylist's best line of the psalm; the blind reader heard "grant what I ask" before "listen" (the cost D3 named, in reverse).

**Ps 5:5 proposes a split:** with a dative or *a dextris* → *pôr-se (diante de / à direita de)* — *De manhã me porei diante de vós e verei* (MS1932's verb; the Greek παραστήσομαί σοι); *me erguerei* after *De manhã* would be heard as getting out of bed. The other places are of this kind (35:5, 44:10b *Ástitit regína a dextris tuis*, 108:31 *ástitit a dextris páuperis*); absolute, as in 2:2, *erguer-se* stays. Passed all three readers.
**Ps 5:9 tests it and it holds:** *Senhor, guiai-me na vossa justiça* (MS1932 and DM1962 both *guia-me*); Latinist clean twice, no remark from stylist or blind reader. Ready to settle.

**Ps 5:9: at the *vós* imperative it is banned** — bare *dirigi* is "I directed", and with the enclitic (*dírige me*, 24:5, 26:11) *dirigi-me* is the everyday "I made my way to". See the new row *dirígere at the vós imperative*.

**Ps 5:12b tests it without Ps 133's support:** *porque vós bendireis ao justo* (dative kept) — the Latinist passed it three times, neither the stylist nor the blind reader remarked on it. It can stand alone; *abençoareis o justo* (MS1932, DM1962) is the option there.
Ps 5:11a *julgai-os, Deus* follows it; the colon is four syllables for the Latin's seven, the first place where *ó Deus* would help the chant (option there). 5:3 *meu Rei e meu Deus*.
Ps 5:11a *júdica illos* → *julgai-os*: heard by the blind reader first as "condemn them" — the Latin's range.

**Ps 5:9 proposes *in conspéctu* + genitive → *à vista de* (*endireitai o meu caminho à vossa vista*)**: keeps this row's noun and the seeing; 51 verses have *in conspéctu* (grep). Tried on 22:5 *Preparastes à minha vista uma mesa*, 137:1b *À vista dos anjos*, 115:15 *Preciosa à vista do Senhor* — it fails none. In Ps 5 it stays apart from *astábo tibi* → *diante de vós* and *ante óculos tuos* → *diante dos vossos olhos*. The blind reader heard "make my conduct right in your eyes" first. Options *na vossa presença*, *diante de vós*.
Ps 5:5 *um Deus que queira a iniquidade* (MS1932 *que ame* refused).
Ps 5:7a *todos os que praticam a iniquidade*; Ps 6:9.

terms: | dirígere at the *vós* imperative | *endireitai* (*endireitai o meu caminho à vossa vista*) | open | Ps 5:9; *dirigi* is also "I directed" (D1/D13), and the enclitic does not save *dírige me* (24:5, 26:11: *dirigi-me* = "I made my way"). *Endireitar* is the verb's first sense (L&S "to lay straight, set in a straight line"), the Greek's (κατεύθυνον), and of the family of *diréctio* → retidão; safe (past *endireitei*). Places: 5:9, 89:16–17, 118:133; with *me* as object (24:5, 26:11) the psalm that meets it decides (*encaminhai-me* is a candidate). Options *tornai reto*; DM1962 *aplainai* is the Hebrew's image. No reader objected |

| pérdere | fazer perecer (*fareis perecer todos os que falam mentira*) | open | Ps 5:7a; the causative of *períre* → perecer, as ἀπόλλυμι is of ἀπόλλυμαι; keeps 72:27 *períbunt: perdidísti* as one figure and stays apart from *dispérdere* → exterminar, its neighbour in 142:12; 7 places (5:7a, 20:11, 25:9, 27:3, 33:17, 72:27, 142:12b), tried in each. The cognate *perdereis* (MS1932) is heard as "you will lose"; *destruir* (DRB) is banned at the *vós* imperative (*destruí*). No reader objected |

| dolus / dolósus / dolóse ágere | engano / enganador / enganar (*o homem de sangue e enganador*; *com as suas línguas enganavam*) | open | Ps 5:7b, 5:11a; 19 verses (*lábia dolósa* 11:3–4, 16:1b, 30:18; *lingua dolósa* 51:6, 108:3, 119:2–3; *dolos* 34:20, 37:13, 49:19; *dolóse egit* 35:3). The cognate *doloso* is criminal law in Brazil. MS1932 has *enganadores* at 54:24. In 5:11a the light verb yields (the Greek has one verb, ἐδολιοῦσαν); *agiam com engano* is the option. **5:11a = 13:3b word for word as far as *agébant*: Ps 13 copies *A sua garganta é um sepulcro aberto, † com as suas línguas enganavam*** |

| vir sánguinum | homem de sangue | open | Ps 5:7b (DM1962's words); the Hebraism kept concrete, the plural lost (as in DRB); 25:9, 54:24 *Viri sánguinum, et dolósi* (→ *Os homens de sangue e enganadores*), 138:19; MS1932 *sanguinário* everywhere |

| multitúdo (+ genitive) | multidão (*na multidão da vossa misericórdia*; *segundo a multidão das suas impiedades*) | open | Ps 5:7b, 5:11b — the psalm sets the two against each other, so one word; 17 verses (50:3b *secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum*; 68:14 = 5:7b's phrase; 36:11 *in multitúdine pacis*; 146:4 *multitúdinem stellárum*). *Abundância* (MS1932 in 5:8) is *abundántia*'s (29:7, 71:7 *abundántia pacis*), *grandeza* *magnitúdo*'s (150:2 has both). Odd with a singular abstract, as the Latin is; no reader stumbled on it — the blind reader heard "because they are many" before "in proportion to" at 5:11b |

| malígnus / malignántes | malvado(s) | open | Ps 5:6 *Nem o malvado habitará junto de vós*. Draft 1 had the cognate: **the blind reader heard *o maligno* first as the devil.** The plural is safe from that (*os malignos*), so 21:17, 25:5, 36:1, 63:3, 91:12, 93:16 may choose; the singular returns in 9:36, 14:4, 100:4. The verb *malignári* (36:8–9, 73:3, 82:4, 104:15) is not settled by this |

| irritáre | provocar (*porque vos provocaram, Senhor*) | open | Ps 5:11b; 10 verses (9:34, 73:10, 105:7, 16, 29, 32, 106:11; the noun in 94:8 *in irritatióne* → *provocação*); L&S quote Nonius: *inritare dictum est proprie provocare*; DRB *provoked*; *irritar* (MS1932) has sunk to "annoy". Stands beside *exacerbáre* in 105:32, 106:11 — proposed *exasperar* there. One collision: 77:58 *provocavérunt*, which can share it |
| abominári | abominar | working | Ps 5:7b; 118:163, 105:40, 106:18 |

| cogitátio | pensamento | working | Ps 5:11b *Caiam dos seus próprios pensamentos* (the image and its openness kept; MS1932 explains: *Frustrem-se os seus desígnios*); family of *cogitáre* → pensar em; 11 verses, God's thoughts included (39:6, 91:6) |

| décidere a | cair de | open | Ps 5:11b; heard by the blind reader first as "be brought down by their own plans", second as "fall away from them" — both are in the Latin; 89:6 *véspere décidat* is the literal sense |
| expéllere | expulsar | working | Ps 5:11b *expulsai-os* (safe: past *expulsei*); 35:13, 43:3 |

| gloriári in | gloriar-se em | open | Ps 5:12b *E em vós se gloriarão* (MS1932 word for word); the blind reader heard "give glory to" before "glory in" and listed *gloriarão* as unknown; kept because the same verb must say the sinners' boasting (51:3, 93:3, 96:7); option *gloriar-se de* |
| dilígere | amar | working | Ps 5:12b *os que amam o vosso nome* |

| bona volúntas | boa vontade | open | Ps 5:13b *com a vossa boa vontade como escudo* — the Latin's two words (εὐδοκία); keeps *volúntas* → vontade and leaves *beneplácito* for *beneplácitum* (10 verses); MS1932 *benevolência* |

| coronáre | coroar | working | Ps 5:13b *nos coroastes*; 8:6 *glória et honóre coronásti eum*, 102:4 (the noun *coróna* 20:4, 64:12); the crown kept though L&S allow "encircle" (*cercar* is *circumdáre*'s) |

| adoráre ad | adorar voltado para | open | Ps 5:8b = 137:2a *adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum* → *adorarei voltado para o vosso templo santo*. The relation (προσκυνήσω πρός) kept against MS1932's *no*. History: *em direção ao* (draft 1; the Latinist's own wording, the stylist heard a route) → *voltando-me para* (draft 2; the Latinist: major, adds an action) → *voltado para* (draft 3, the stylist's; gate clean). **Cost: a masculine participle the Latin does not have** — whoever rules should weigh *em direção ao*, the genderless fall-back |
| mane | de manhã | working | Ps 5:4–5, twice as the Latin |
| clamor | clamor | working | Ps 5:2; family of *clamáre* |
| orátio / oráre | oração / orar | working | Ps 5:3–4 *da minha oração … a vós orarei* (the Latin's echo; MS1932 *súplica* is *deprecátio*'s) |
| mendácium, *loqui mendácium* | mentira, *falar mentira* | working | Ps 5:7a |
| impíetas | impiedade | working | Ps 5:11b; listed as unknown by the blind reader (so was *iniquidade*); kept |
formulas: | *Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum, † linguis suis dolóse agébant* (5:11a = 13:3b) | *A sua garganta é um sepulcro aberto, † com as suas línguas enganavam* | working — Ps 5; Ps 13 copies it (hangs on *dolus*) |
| *in multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ* (5:7b = 68:14) | *na multidão da vossa misericórdia* | open (hangs on *multitúdo*) — Ps 5 |
| *adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum* (5:8b = 137:2a) | *adorarei voltado para o vosso templo santo* | open (hangs on *adoráre ad*) — Ps 5 |
| *Rex meus et Deus meus* (5:3, 43:5, 83:4) | *meu Rei e meu Deus* | working — Ps 5 |
